steps.what: Take the patient's medical history and capture relevant facts
Draft the medical history in the patient record

loop.purpose: Produce a faithful history note from the technician's brief
loop.input: Captured history facts with reported uncertainty
loop.output: Draft history note with gaps flagged
loop.check: Technician compares symptoms, timing, medication names, allergies and negations with the captured facts; no unreported finding may be inserted
loop.stop: One correction pass, then manual note entry for unresolved facts
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative history varies; field substitution alone cannot preserve meaning

steps.what: Verify and file the history note for clinical review

tasks.design: Use a draft facility within {OTHER}, the clinical record, after the technician captures the history. Keep patient questioning, meaning checks and final filing human; the draft cannot create a diagnosis or treatment instruction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative facts must be rewritten into a clinical note.
tasks.enabler_now: Consultation-summary drafting exists, though local history-note gains require measurement.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain recollections and clinically significant negatives.
tasks.human_edge: The technician asks follow-up questions and recognises incomplete history.
tasks.altitude: Less note composition while patient contact and filing responsibility stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber summarises consultations into clinical records. This supports documentation drafting, not shorter ophthalmic history interviews or the exact brief-based design.

assumptions: Boundary is taking and documenting history, excluding examination and clinical diagnosis.

Technician produces the history brief in s1: patient and encounter identifiers, presenting concern, onset, laterality, relevant medical history, medicines, allergies and reported uncertainty. The full 60 hours include brief entry or dictation; no free recording or structured feed is assumed.
Missing history is clarified manually in s1; draft gaps are resolved in s2. No ambient recording is required.
Test native clinical templates first. Three focal quality-sampling hours and two other-role access-maintenance hours are additional per 100 baseline hours.
research_questions: Does drafting save time after brief capture, corrections and final filing?

incremental.description: Sample note quality and review template changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact final history note, patient and encounter identifiers; edits require renewed verification

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60+15+15=90; gross 10 less 3 upkeep gives net 7. Low 1 allows six extra correction hours for uncertain histories. Interview time stays unchanged; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Measure lens power using the lensometer and identify the patient and lens
Record measured lens power in the clinical record
Verify patient, laterality and recorded lens measurements before filing

tasks.design: Use the supported connection between {OTHER}, the lensometer, and the clinical record to stage measured values. The technician still performs the measurement, links the correct patient and lens, and checks the result before filing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values may be manually transcribed from an instrument display.
tasks.enabler_now: Supported device interfaces can transfer numerical measurements without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable measurement and correct patient and laterality association.
tasks.human_edge: The technician positions and checks the lens and recognises implausible results.
tasks.altitude: Remove transcription where a supported device interface exists; measurement responsibility stays unchanged.

reach.learn: Device interface and measurement quality controls

evidence.claim: Supported instrument-to-record numerical transfer is deterministic; applicability to the installed lensometer is an E1 assumption, not a digest-verified product claim.

assumptions: Boundary is measurement and recording of existing lens power, excluding refraction and prescription decisions.

Technician produces patient identifier, encounter identifier, lens side and measurement acceptance in s1; lensometer produces sphere, cylinder, axis, addition where applicable, units, timestamp and device identifier. The unchanged 80 hours include patient linking and repeat measurements.
s2 only stages values. Missing identifiers or unsupported device output require manual entry and a lower saving; no extraction service is assumed free.

Test native certified device integration first. Four focal interface-check hours and two other-role support hours are additional per 100 baseline hours. If values already transfer automatically, decline deployment and claim no new saving.
research_questions: Can supported transfer preserve patient, laterality and units while eliminating manual entry?

already_counted.description: Check transferred values and file result

incremental.description: Test device-result mappings and review transfer failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, encounter, lens side, units and measurement values; any alteration voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=80+0+5=85; gross 15 less 4 focal upkeep gives net 11 where transcription exists. Low 0 represents no viable new transfer saving and no deployment. Physical measurement retains 80 hours; E1.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach contact lens care and use

steps.what: Instruct patients in contact lens care and check their handling technique

tasks.design: Retain direct teaching and observation of the patient's contact lens technique. Approved guidance in {DOCS} can support instruction without assuming a shorter hands-on session.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patients need demonstration, practice and individual correction.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable guidance supports consistency but does not verify technique.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe handling and responding to dexterity or comprehension difficulties.
tasks.human_edge: The technician watches practice and adapts teaching immediately.
tasks.altitude: Teaching time and responsibilities remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Contact lens instruction requires observation and correction of the patient's physical technique.

assumptions: Boundary is teaching and checking technique, excluding separate prescribing and record writing.
No machine step or structured competence flag is assumed; technician observes handling during the full-time session.
Check existing approved guidance before creating tools.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new instructional system is deployed.
research_questions: Do existing visual aids improve technique without reducing necessary supervised practice?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0. Hands-on teaching and observation are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Call patients about post-operative recovery and escalate concerning responses

tasks.design: Keep the recovery call with the technician using {TELEPHONY}. Clinical questions, clarification and escalation remain personal work; a reminder service is outside this conversation boundary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recovery accounts can be incomplete and concerning symptoms need clarification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing telephone tools support contact but do not establish a shorter clinical conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising concerning responses and reaching patients who do not answer.
tasks.human_edge: The technician hears uncertainty and seeks help promptly within the care protocol.
tasks.altitude: No change in call time or escalation responsibility.

evidence.claim: Post-operative follow-up calls include contextual questioning and escalation; reminders alone do not replace that work.

assumptions: Boundary is calling and discussing recovery, excluding scheduling and separate record composition.
Treating clinician produces follow-up instructions during existing care planning; contact details come from existing registration. No new structured symptom feed or automatic triage is introduced.
Unreadable or missing instructions are clarified manually during the retained call workflow.
Use existing telephone facilities first. Zero incremental upkeep because the call process is unchanged.
research_questions: Which observed follow-up delays arise outside the actual recovery conversation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0. No unobserved scheduling or documentation saving is added to the clinical call.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Preserve patient-facing care and physical measurements, reducing only verified documentation and transcription work.
reach: Coordinate record quality with medical records specialists
role.ambitious_version: A technician with accurate records and protected time for patient instruction and recovery conversations.
